stem:
Padma writes $56=14\times 4$ and $63=21\times 3$. She asks whether that single pair of factorisations proves $56$ and $63$ have no common factor greater than $1$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Conclude they are co-prime from those two products alone, without checking whether another common factor was missed.
Say that calling them co-prime is what creates the incomplete factor listing, instead of testing all possible common factors.
No: one chosen factorisation of each number can miss a common factor; the search must account for every possible common factor.
Require a full prime-factorisation write-up of every integer as the only allowed method for this decision.

teacher.key_rationale: One factor pair can miss a shared factor; proving no common factor other than $1$ needs a search that covers all possibilities. Treating one pair as enough, reversing conclusion and listing, or demanding a later full prime-factorisation procedure all miss that hinge.
